headline: BGB foils push-in attempt of 8 people at Kushtia border
summary: Border Guard Bangladesh prevented a group of two men, four women, and two transgender persons from entering the country via a river.
details: The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has foiled an alleged attempt by India's Border Security Force (BSF) to push eight people into Bangladesh through the border in Kushtia's Daulatpur upazila.

caption:
8 people tried to swim across the border river into Bangladesh—but the BGB was waiting.

The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has foiled an alleged attempt by India's Border Security Force (BSF) to push eight people into Bangladesh through the border in Kushtia's Daulatpur upazila.

The incident occurred around 5:10 am today near border pillar 152/1-S under the Jaypur Border Outpost (BOP) of the BGB-47 Kushtia Battalion.

According to the BGB, members of the BSF's Char Meghna Camp allegedly tried to send the eight individuals into Bangladesh by making them swim across a river.

The group consisted of two men, four women, and two transgender persons.

A BGB patrol immediately detected the attempt and prevented the group from entering the country.

Due to the firm stance of the BGB and local residents, the group was forced to swim back to the Indian side of the river.
